![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14202292/assets/d9e89a9b811bdc6b766b01eecf817df48968e3ea604b89bc55bc9660331194e0.png)

Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above? 

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=4$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,3}f(x)=1$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=3\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=3.$

- Statement II is true. Both limits ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)$ do not exist because the function $f(x)$ is not given in the interval $(0,2].$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$

- Statement III is true. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{+}}f(x)=1\,.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,3}f(x)=1.$

In conclusion, only statements II and III are true.
